item.title: Mike McCarthy responds to Aaron Rodgers leaking Packers cheer in Steelers game: ‘Embarrassing moment’
item.description: Mike McCarthy responds to Aaron Rodgers leaking Packers cheer in Steelers game: ‘Embarrassing moment’ originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers officially released quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, following an appearance that Rodgers made on ESPN that was anything but boring. During an interview with ESPN's Pat McAfee , Rodgers called head coach Mike McCarthy "unhealthy" and rattled off hordes of reasons he was unhappy with the coach. Rodgers even claimed that McCarthy fell asleep during team meetings and missing walk-throughs. "Last Thursday, I was in a quarterback meeting and in 10 minutes I heard snoring," Rodgers said. "Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting. Friday, he misses walk-through... Saturday, he misses the team meeting." One of the craziest accusations was that McCarthy led a "‘1, 2, 3, Packers " chant during the Steelers' game against the Eagles . NFL insider Jordan Schultz says this is true , and McCarthy was asked about it during a presser on Wednesday. Mike McCarthy reacts to Aaron Rodgers' accusations of a Green Bay Packers cheer during a Pittsburgh Steelers game When asked about that accusation of the chant, McCarthy responded and seemed to admit it happened. "The Philadelphia situation at halftime was very emotional," McCarthy said, according to USA Today . "There's conversations prior to that. Embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments." He added, "Aaron and I have a long history. He has a lot of opinions, and those are things we always talked about. Once again, I consider those private conversations." McCarthy also confirmed that Pittsburgh released Rodgers during that presser. Now, Rodgers is a free agent, and he'll either take that as a sign to officially retire to land elsewhere. item.title: Bruno Fernandes weighs in on Senne Lammens errors after Man United drop Champions League points
item.description: Bruno Fernandes scored twice as Manchester United drew 2-2 with Sporting CP -Credit:Gualter Fatia - UEFA, UEFA via Getty Images Bruno Fernandes reassured Senne Lammens that "mistakes are part of football" following the goalkeeper's two costly errors against Sporting Lisbon in the UEFA Champions League. Lammens conceded a penalty in the first half, charging out of his area to bring down Sporting defender Maximiliano Araújo, before fumbling a cross to gift the home side their equalizer in the 80th minute. United appeared set to snatch victory when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira bundled the ball into his own net, only for VAR to disallow the goal after Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have fouled him. Alejandro Garnacho casts doubt over Aston Villa future after taking drastic action Tim Weah won't 'beg' for USMNT return after Mauricio Pochettino snubbed Marseille captain -Credit:PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA, AFP via Getty Images "I think we started the game very well," Fernandes told TNT Sports, via the Manchester Evening News . "Then we gave up the way we set it up. We were in full control of the game with the ball very well. We gave one or two counters, but we were very good in recovering the positions. "Then they get the goal. I think we were still in control of the game, probably not creating as much as we wanted. We didn't have enough people in the last third. We arrived with only one or two players, that was difficult. "Then in the second half we get the two goals and I think there was the moment where we should have pushed a little bit more and it was the other way around. We sit a little bit. We were a little bit afraid of the moment also probably and we end up conceding another goal." Asked about Lammens' mistakes, he said: "It's part of football. Mistakes are part of football and from that you get goals, but obviously it's not an individual sport, so everyone has to take the blame for everything we do good and everything we do bad. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "So I think the main thing and the most important thing is that we understand that we need to be in this together in the good and in the bad moments and it's not going to change the belief we have in each other." Fernandes also revealed that Mauricio Pochettino urged his players to push further forward following the first half. "He wanted more aggression, more bodies up front, more runs," said Fernandes. "I think the first goal comes from that, I mean, it comes from a run from behind. We said the run from the second line was important for us because they couldn't catch that. "They have a very high line. It was difficult for the front players to get onside. So from the second line, me, Youri [Tielemans], we should have done a little bit more. We did it in the first half at spells, but not enough. In the second half, we started doing it more, and we created a lot of danger, and it led to the two goals for us."

item.title: Scorned AD reportedly suing Michigan despite getting over $17 million for not working
item.description: Credit: Vasha Hunt-Imagn Images On Tuesday, the University of Michigan announced that, despite earlier reports that it had landed on Trev Alberts as its next athletic director, the university would not be proceeding with the hire. “The University of Michigan’s search for its next athletic director is ongoing,” Michigan spokesperson Paul Corliss said in a statement. “As we navigate a rapidly changing landscape in intercollegiate athletics, the values that define Michigan will guide our decisions and reinforce our commitment to excellence and integrity, both in the classroom and in competition.” The decision was reportedly made after the school’s regents became aware of Alberts’ answers during a deposition during his tenure as the AD for the University of Nebraska. Former Nebraska Cornhuskers women’s basketball player Ashley Scoggin sued the Nebraska Board of Regents, the women’s basketball coach, and then-AD Trev Alberts in February 2024, after she was dismissed from the team due to a sexual relationship with assistant coach Chuck Love. During a deposition with Scoggin’s lawyers, Alberts was asked if it was permissible for students and coaches to be involved sexually and answered, in part, that “it just depends.” Alberts’ answer likely held more weight with Michigan’s brass than it would with other schools due to its former head coach, Sherrone Moore, being fired for cause after it was determined that he had an inappropriate sexual relationship with a football staffer. All the same, following Michigan’s decision not to hire him after learning about his answer, Alberts is now suing, according to The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman. “Trev Alberts plans to file a lawsuit against the University of Michigan and perhaps incoming president C. Cybele Raver after the university rescinded his job offer earlier this week, his attorney Tom Mars told @TheAthletic,” Feldman reported. Alberts response is somewhat surprising, considering that reports indicate that he signed a MOU with Michigan last week that will ensure he gets paid over $17 million despite his offer being rescinded, as well as the multi-million amount that he owes Texas A&M for departing the school, with which he held the same role. item.title: Unpacking every crazy moment from Sporting-Man United
item.description: Three penalties, two disallowed goals, one fluke, and a “main-character energy” referee: Manchester United ’s 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League had a bit of everything. Mauricio Pochettino was denied his first win as United manager as his side saw a late winner disallowed by VAR in a bonkers clash in Lisbon. Referee Szymon Marciniak was in the thick of the action throughout and in the 84th minute ruled that Patrick Dorgu had fouled Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira, who let a corner from Bruno Fernandes slip through his fingers. But that was not all - here’s a breakdown of all the main incidents from a crazy night. 32’ Man United concede two penalties in three minutes (SPO 1-0 MUN) After a subdued start in Lisbon, Mauricio Pochettino saw his new defence implode as they conceded two penalties in the space of three minutes. The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg. If it appeared soft, justice was perhaps served when Senne Lammens saved a tame effort from Sporting striker Luis Suarez low down to his left. But in farcical scenes, Lammens then conceded another penalty just 75 seconds later when he crashed into Maximiliano Araujo in the box. Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row. It was the first time United had conceded two penalties in the same Champions League match since 1998, while they have now conceded five in total in all competitions this season. And Lammens went from hero to zero as he undid his penalty save by quickly conceding another. Man Utd are behind in Lisbon 😬 Luis Suárez converts from the spot at the second attempt moments after Senne Lammens saved his first 💥 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/BqDPDsRJc7 — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 25, 2026 42’ Amad Diallo goal disallowed: Why did the referee whistle? (SPO 1-0 MUN) Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled that Youri Tielemans had committed a foul on Goncalo Inacio when he slid to poke the ball through to Amad Diallo, who headed into an empty net at the second attempt after the goalkeeper deflected his shot onto the crossbar. However, because Marciniak had already blown his whistle to stop play following the challenge from Tielemans, VAR could not intervene. Tielemans did not appear to commit a foul and instead won the ball fairly against Inacio when he went to ground to play the ball through to Amad. If Marciniak hadn’t blown for the foul, the VAR would have been able to allow it, if they had ruled that Tielemans had not fouled Inacio. “It was a dreadful decision,” former United midfielder Owen Hargreaves said on TNT Sports. “I don’t know what [the referee] saw. item.title: "Now isn't the time" - Kompany avoids finger pointing as Bayern suffer first defeat
item.description: "Now isn't the time" - Kompany avoids finger pointing as Bayern suffer first defeat On the 18th attempt, Bayern Munich suffered their first defeat of the campaign on Wednesday, with Lille securing a 2-1 win in the Champions League. Making the trip to northern France, Vincent Kompany's depleted side took the lead via Dayot Upamecano in the 15th minute, and strolled into half-time carrying a deserved 1-0 lead. But, the hosts would flip the clash on its head in the second half, with Ayase Ueda's equaliser followed by an own-goal from Aleksandar Pavlovic just minutes later, condemning Der Rekordmeister to their first defeat since April. Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, boss Kompany reflected on what was most definitely a tale of two halves. “The first half was pretty much how we'd envisioned our game would go,” said the Belgian, after his side strutted their stuff with relative ease despite operating with a depleted 11. "It highlighted both our strengths and our weaknesses. But overall, it was a good first half. "In the second half, we just couldn't find our rhythm anymore, And then, of course, you don't have that breathing room, that space where you're so far ahead that the game is already decided. That's part of football. Of course, you have to play the game until the very end. “We tried. So, that's that, there's no blame to be placed on anyone, but the second goal, of course, shouldn't have happened," he added, referencing Pavlovic's own goal in which the midfielder will not want to see again when analysing the defeat. However, the Bayern boss insisted that the blame game is far from the right path to take in this instance. “From experience, I know these moments. I know that now isn't the time; we have to fight for our chances, stick together, fight for it and enjoy the battle; that's part of it." With the club reviving the ‘FC Hollywood’ tag as a result of recent events, Kompany has the task of steadying the ship as the winter break approaches, and with a trip to Hamburg coming at the weekend, the German champions will be looking for a response to their first loss of the season, potentially easing the tension surrounding the club at this moment in time.

item.title: A Toothpaste Marketer Turned an Energy Drink Into Two F1 Teams Valued at $8.65 Billion
item.description: Red Bull’s founder Dietrich Mateschitz went from marketing toothpaste to owning two F1 teams that Sportico now values at a combined $8.65 billion. It started with a case of jet lag. Mateschitz, who worked in marketing for the German consumer-goods company Blendax, bought a bottle of a Thai tonic called Krating Daeng on the way from Bangkok airport into the city. “One glass and the jet lag was gone,” he later recalled, according to Wikipedia’s account of his life . From a Thai Tonic to a Grand Prix Grid In 1984, he and the drink’s Thai creator, Chaleo Yoovidhya, each put in $500,000 to start Red Bull, with 49% apiece. Red Bull launched in Austria in 1987. Formula 1 came next. Ford sold him its struggling Jaguar team in November 2004, reportedly for a single dollar. BBC Sport reported at the time that Ford wanted a symbolic dollar and a commitment to invest $400 million in the team over three seasons. It raced as Red Bull Racing from 2005. A second team followed in September 2005, when Mateschitz and Gerhard Berger bought Minardi. It became Toro Rosso in 2006, and today it races as Racing Bulls. Sebastian Vettel’s Toro Rosso at Monza in 2008, the year he won there. Image Credit: Jane Belinda Smith / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0) Winning With the Junior Team First The little team scored the first big payoff. Sebastian Vettel took Toro Rosso to victory at Monza in 2008, on a wet day, and was promoted to the senior team soon after. Red Bull Racing has since won six constructors’ championships, in 2010 to 2013 and in 2022 and 2023, and eight drivers’ titles: four for Vettel from 2010 to 2013 and four for Max Verstappen from 2021 to 2024. The money has kept pace. In its November 2026 rankings, Sportico values Red Bull at $5.6 billion, fourth among the 11 teams and up 30% on a year ago. It puts Racing Bulls at $3.05 billion, up 49%. Together, that makes $8.65 billion for a business that began with a pair of $500,000 checks. Mateschitz died in October 2022, but both teams are still part of the company he built.

item.title: Bayern Munich stunned 2-1 by Lille in Champions League after second half collapse
item.description: (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images It’s all gone from bad to worse for Bayern Munich as the German Rekordmeister fell to a 2-1 loss to Lille in France in the Champions League. The result comes just a few short days after the disappointing 1-1 draw with FC Köln in the Bundeslig a, a match in which Bayern lost both Harry Kane and Michael Olise to injury in the first half, with Kane facing a long spell on the sidelines. Against Lille, Vincent Kompany started an attacking four of Lennart Karl, Tom Bischof, Nathaniel Brown, and Konrad Laimer. He really didn’t have many other options with Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, and Ismael Saibari all out injured, and both Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz starting on the bench after returning from lengthy injury layoffs. Bayern looked to be in control of the match even with an injury-hit squad, taking a 1-0 lead into halftime on a Dayot Upamecano header off a Bischof corner. Konrad Laimer missed a gilt-edged chance to make it 2-0 for the Bundesliga champions, leaving Bayern with a narrow lead at the break despite controlling 60% of possession and putting at least five shots on target. In the second half, Lille dealt Bayern a one-two sucker punch in the 62nd and 65th minutes, scoring through Ayase Ueda and an unfortunate own goal from Aleksandar Pavlović as he tried to clear a shot that had come off the post. The midfielder falling to his knees and burying his face in his palms captured Bayern’s frustration on a night when the club conceded twice in three minutes and left Lille empty-handed. Speaking after the match, Laimer offered his assessment and said Bayern lost too much of the control and momentum it had in the first 45 minutes. “I thought we had a very decent first half, in which we implemented many of the things we had set out to do. I think we were very aggressive, had good energy, won a lot of duels, and picked up a lot of second balls. But we lost a bit of that in the second half. Then we conceded two goals, and things became far too easy for them. We also failed to produce the level of performance we are capable of. And now we’re standing here with zero points,” the Austr ian said (via @iMiaSanMia ). Bayern now finds itself in 15th place in the Champions League table, needing results to climb back into the top eight for automatic knockout-stage qualification. With its next two matches in the competition coming against Slavia Prague and a struggling Manchester United squad, Bayern should have a chance to turn things around—though nothing is guaranteed. That’s the nature of the Champions League, a point Laimer underscored. “That’s Champions League football. That’s how it is. Now it’s simply about recovering quickly because we’re going through a very intense period with very little time between games,” he stressed. Join the conversation! item.title: How Does Gabe Vincent Signing Impact the Kings?
item.description: On Sunday, Nov. 22, the Sacramento Kings signed veteran point guard Gabe Vincent to a one-year, non-guaranteed deal. The move comes after it became increasingly apparent that Malik Monk was not cutting it as a backup point guard. The Kings have played Monk less and less as the season has progressed because their offense is poor with him on the floor. Vincent slotting into the Kings’ lineup as backup point guard shifts Monk to a secondary ball-handling role, where he has been more comfortable in the past. He also provides continuity behind rookie Darius Acuff Jr. , a player the organization sees as their superstar of the future. Vincent is a Savvy Player Acuff is third in the NBA in minutes per game, averaging 36.6. It is unprecedented for a rookie to lead that category, but the coaching staff has deemed it necessary to play him so much. With Acuff off the floor, turnovers increase, offensive possessions stall, and players take poor shots. Vincent represents stability; he makes wise decisions with the ball. His numbers don’t jump off the stat sheet — Vincent averaged just 3.9 points, 1.6 assists, and 1.1 rebounds in 13.3 minutes per game. What does stand out, however, is his minuscule 0.6 turnovers per game. The 1.6-to-0.6 assist-to-turnover ratio means he averages 2.67 assists for every singular turnover. Monk’s ratio is 3.6-to-1.69, meaning he averages 2.11 assists before turning the ball over. Vincent doesn’t play himself off the floor; he does what the coaching staff asks of him in his minutes. One could categorize his play style as boring, but Kings fans would much prefer boring over unpredictable. At this point in his career, Gabe Vincent does exactly one thing well: handle the ball without turning it over. A perfectly safe, boring, dependable ball-handler. The Kings have clearly had enough of the Monk backup PG experience and opted for his exact opposite. https://t.co/fkJsWbAGrB — Jack Dann (@JackBDann) November 22, 2026 Looking beyond his offensive impact, Vincent is not a liability on defense. When engaged, he’s a solid point-of-attack defender who plays with hustle and physicality. Monk is lack-luster defensively, so Vincent has a leg up on him there. Even if Vincent’s shot isn’t falling on a given night, he can ensure the second unit doesn’t completely lose the game. Vincent Provides Mentorship Vincent’s journey to the NBA was anything but easy. After completing his college career at UC Santa Barbara, Vincent entered the NBA Draft, but went undrafted. He wound up playing for his hometown Stockton Kings in the NBA G League. item.title: Joe Burrow 'certainly' surprised by Steelers' release of Aaron Rodgers
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said Nov. 25 that he thinks the Pittsburgh Steelers' release of future Pro Football Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers was unexpected, but didn't say much else about it. "I don't know much about the situation," Burrow said . "Certainly surprising, but I guess I don't know much." Burrow was asked whether it could be good for the Bengals' playoff hopes that Rodgers was released. "I don't know," Burrow said. "We'll see." About one hour earlier, the Steelers announced they released Rodgers during what's believed to be his 22nd and final NFL season after a very public rift with head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow met on the field after Cincinnati's 38-18 rout of Pittsburgh on NBC's Sunday Night Football. "That was a clinic out there, kid," Rodgers told Burrow as they shook hands. "Good job, keep rolling." "Thank you, bro," Burrow responded. "If this is your last one, much love and respect." In a postgame interview on the field with Melissa Stark, Burrow talked about his respect for Rodgers. "I just have a lot of respect for him and what he's done," Burrow said . "He's such a good player and continues to play at a high level at 40-whatever he is," Burrow told reporters . "Somebody that I loved watching growing up. Really second to none as far as throwing the football and really still is. Just have a lot of appreciation for what he's brought to the game and all the things that he's done." Burrow was unable to break a record held by Pro Football Hall of Famer Peyton Manning during the team's NFL Week 11 loss to the Washington Commanders on ESPN's Monday Night Football at Northwest Stadium. Burrow finished the game with two touchdowns. He was seeking a sixth straight game with at least four passing/rushing TDs. Burrow enters the Bengals' NFL Week 12 game against the New Orleans Saints needing one touchdown pass to match Boomer Esiason for third place in Bengals' franchise history. item.title: Isak 'in a good place' as Liverpool close on Champions League last 16
item.description: Alexander Isak scored twice in Liverpool's 3-0 win over Club Brugge (NICOLAS TUCAT) Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz fired Liverpool towards the Champions League last 16 with an impressive 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday. Both star forwards struggled to justify their price tags during a difficult first season, but are beginning to show why they cost nearly a combined £250 million ($327 million) to bring them to Anfield last year. Isak's cool finish opened the scoring and the Swede then rounded off a fine night for Andoni Iraola's men with his 10th goal of the season. Moments earlier Wirtz had netted for the fifth consecutive game for club and country with a sublime finish. "Perfect away win, I would say," Isak told TNT Sports. "I'm in a good place and the team is in a good place, most importantly. Hopefully, it gets better from here. "The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations and whoever comes in, we have a dangerous attack. It feels good." Victory takes Liverpool up to fifth in the Champions League table and closing in on a top-eight finish that will secure a place in the last 16. "An important game for us at a key moment in the group stage," said Iraola. "It puts us in a good position, guarantees qualification for the knockout stage, but now we want to go to the top eight." Brugge began the night level on points with the six-time European champions, but failed to score for the first time in 38 games to slip down to 13th. Liverpool were able to cruise to a 4-0 win over Manchester United with a man advantage for over 80 minutes at the weekend. But Iraola still took the chance to rest captain Virgil van Dijk, Alexis Mac Allister and teenage sensation Rio Ngumoha with one eye on Sunday's Merseyside derby at Everton. - Sommer error opens door - Brugge's experienced goalkeeper Yann Sommer handed Liverpool the breakthrough when his poor pass was pounced on by Bradley Barcola, who teed up Dominik Szoboszlai to cross for Isak to tap in the opener on 13 minutes. Ngumoha was forced into action before half-time after Victor Munoz hobbled off in the only setback of the night for Liverpool. Sommer made amends with a brilliant stop to deny Szoboszlai as Liverpool pressed to double their advantage after the break. The second goal arrived 11 minutes from time when Ngumoha wriggled free to tee up Wirtz on the edge of the box. Wirtz has credited former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp for helping him to find top form during the international break with Germany. His newfound confidence was on show as he curled a fine strike in off the inside of the post to end any hope of a Brugge revival. Isak then pounced on a long punt forward by Alisson Becker to spring in behind the Belgians' defence and delicately lift the ball over Sommer as Liverpool made amends for a shock defeat to Fenerbahce last time out in the Champions League. kca/mw

item.title: QB Rodgers released by Steelers after slamming coach McCarthy
item.description: FILE PHOTO - A view of the NFL logo on the pitch before the 2026 NFL Game between Atalanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals at the Santiago Bernabéu. (is associated with: «QB Rodgers released by Steelers after slamming coach McCarthy») Nathalia Araújo/dpa The Pittsburgh Steelers have waived Aaron Rodgers after the quarterback slammed coach Mike McCarthy on Wednesday. Rodgers was benched ahead of the NFL game against the Denver Broncos on Friday and said during The Pat McAfeee Show that he wouldn't return to the team. "That ship has sailed," Rodgers said of his time with the Steelers. He explained that he found out from team-mate Pat Freiermuth that he was being benched in favour of Mason Rudolph, and that he still hasn't heard the news from McCarthy. He then went on to recount that McCarthy was "snoring" in team meetings and that what happened this week was not "abnormal." "Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened," Rodgers said. He added that the issues with the coach go back to training camp during summer and revealed that McCarthy broke down the team at half-time of their 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles last Sunday with "one, two, three, Packers." "And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at half-time, towards the end of it (...) And there's some rambling or something, and without even a heads-up, he says, 'All right, one, two, three, (Green Bay) Packers.'" Since Rodgers' release happened after the league's trade deadline, he's available to be claimed by any other team on waivers. If he goes unclaimed, he will become an unrestricted free agent. The quarterback won the Super Bowl in 2011 with the Packers - back then coached by McCarthy - and was named the NFL most valuable player four times (2011, 2014, 2020 and 2021). McCarthy took the Steelers coaching job this year after Mike Tomlin resigned following 19 seasons in the position.

item.title: Bill Simmons reveals how he would react if New England Patriots sign Aaron Rodgers
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ career with the Pittsburgh Steelers is over. But there is still a possibility he plays in the NFL again. After an explosive interview attacking Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers has been waived by the team. There will now be an opportunity for quarterback-needy NFL teams to negotiate with Rodgers and bring him in to try and save their season. One of these could be the New England Patriots, who have just lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to a fractured ankle. Patriots fan Bill Simmons said he would ultimately welcome a move. He wrote on X: “Just so you know — if the Pats signed Rodgers I’d talk myself into it before our turkey is carved tomorrow.” Options for Rodgers The New England Patriots are currently planning to start Tommy DeVito for the rest of the season, which does not fill many fans with a lot of confidence. Another option could be for Rodgers to sign for the Steelers’ rivals the Baltimore Ravens, who are set to play Pittsburgh twice still. The Ravens have lost six straight games and recently traded for Jacoby Brissett, but Rodgers could be an upgrade. A further option could be the New York Giants, if they believe he can be an instant upgrade on JJ McCarthy. But it is still unclear if Rodgers wants to play again, after a dramatic 24 hours. item.description: Photo by Getty Images | ﻿Photo by Getty Images Bayern Munich created chaos for the first 45 minutes in the Champions League clash against Lille. Dayot Upamecano scored a header from a well-designed set piece an d gave Bayern a lead heading into the locker room at halftime. In the second half, Bayern made sloppy passes, reacted too slowly in defensive situations, and ultimately ran out of steam and ideas against the French side. In the postgame interview (via @iMiaSanMia ), Bayern manager Vincent Kompany analyzed the tale of two halves. “The first half was definitely very much what we had envisaged for this game,” said Kompany. “We showed our strengths, but also some of our weaknesses. Overall, though, it was a good first half. Then, in the second half, we simply couldn’t get back into our rhythm. And naturally, that means you no longer have the same fre edom and space to play as well as you would like and see the game through comfortably.” Kompany insisted, “That’s part of football, of course. You have to play your game right until the final minute. We tried. It’s not a question of energy or anything like that, and there are no accusations in that regard. The second goal, of course, should never have happened. But as I said, I know these situations from ex perience. I know what this means now. We have to fight to regain our momentum. Stick together, fight, and even enjoy that battle a little. That’s part of it.” Bayern will need to be more consistent for the final month of 2026. item.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany was forced to improvise due to a wave of injuries. (Francois LO PRESTI) Bayern Munich suffered their first defeat of the season on Wednesday, losing 2-1 at Lille in the Champions League as a tough week for the German giants worsened. Dayot Upamecano opened the scoring for Bayern but Ayase Ueda levelled for Lille before a horror Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal gifted the hosts victory. Bayern were the only club in Europe's top-five leagues yet to have lost a match in any competition this season but came unstuck against a Lille side who entered the game second last in the table. The defeat continued a terrible past few days for Bayern, who lost star striker Harry Kane for several months to a serious ankle injury on Friday and then had Michael Olise ruled out with a foot complaint. Coach Vincent Kompany, who himself returned this week after a month out with meningeal irritation, brought Jamal Musiala off the bench for the last 15 minutes. Musiala has found himself in the headlines this week after several members of Bayern's hierarchy called for the 23-year-old to take a pay cut as he battles his way back from a neurological condition, drawing fierce condemnation from players' unions. "I know these moments from experience," Kompany said to DAZN. "I know what this is like. Now, we have to fight to create our own moments. "We need to stick together, fight, and even learn to enjoy the struggle -- that's all part of it. "There are no excuses. It's simply the reality we face, and we have to stand together." The defeat in France left Bayern 15th in the Champions League table with three games remaining, while Lille's first win moved them to within two points of the knockout places. "This game didn't decide the Champions League," Kompany said. "PSG didn't even reach the top eight in the last two years and remember they won the Champions League back-to-back." - Karl fills in up front - Bayern's forward line included just one recognised forward in 18-year-old winger Lennart Karl. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As much as I would have loved to see Dylan Larkin in a Minnesota Wild jersey, I can’t blame general manager Bill Guerin if he wasn’t willing to give up what the Montreal Canadiens did to get him. TSN’s Pierre LeBrun has brought up three names Bill Guerin could turn his attention to after missing out on Larkin: Ryan O’Reilly, Pavel Zacha and Evgeni Malkin. All three could become unrestricted free agents next summer. Ryan O’Reilly Would Be a Great Fit in Minnesota If I’m Guerin, O’Reilly is the guy I’m calling about. He’s spent most of his career playing against some of the best players in the NHL, he’s great in the faceoff circle and he can still produce offensively. item.title: Lesson learned? 49ers' Nick Bosa practices brevity after drawing boos in Mexico City
item.description: San Francisco 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa reacts to a penalty called on him in a game against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026 in Mexico City. (Gregory Payan/Associated Press) A week after Nick Bosa unwittingly offended a vocal segment of one of the world's largest cities, it sounded as if the San Francisco 49ers ' All-Pro pass rusher had learned a lesson from the experience: say less. On Wednesday, three days after Bosa inspired boos and whistles before the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings in front of a crowd of 85,612 in Mexico City, he kept his answers brief when asked about the unwelcoming reception. "I definitely didn't mean any harm with my comments," Bosa said. Was that the message Bosa was trying to convey with the heart gesture he gave to the fans? "The intentions were pure," Bosa said. Later, when a reporter who was late to Bosa's group interview at his locker broached the topic, Bosa didn't engage. "I already talked about it," he said. Last week, Bosa was more verbose when he was asked about the Mexico City crowd during the 49ers' 38-10 win over the Cardinals in 2022. "I think we need some information given to fans so they know when to cheer," Bosa said. "Because they just chant the whole time. If we can kind of teach them - no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques - but if they can cheer when we're on defense, that would be great." For those who booed Bosa when he appeared on the big screen during warmups, his comments were clearly taken as a shot at the country's sports heritage. It was noted by a reporter that Bosa was cheered during the game. "All the interactions that I had face-to-face were amazing," he said. Bosa previously irritated a segment of a country in October 2024, about a week before the presidential election, when he crashed an NBC interview wearing a "Make American Great Again" hat after a win over the Cowboys. Bosa was fined $11,255 by the NFL – after Donald Trump beat Kamala Harris. "It was well worth it," Bosa said of the fine. "Clearly, the nation spoke." After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
